executive_summary: EUR/AUD trades at 1.61459 as of the 2026-09-03 close, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date, and it sits at the 0th percentile of its 52-week closing range — 6.5 pips above the lowest close of the past year at 1.61394, set on 13 May 2026. The pair has fallen 1.38% over one month, 1.37% over three months, 0.18% over six months and 9.03% over twelve, and it is below every moving average in the stack: the 50-day at 1.63603 (-1.31%), the 100-day at 1.63408 (-1.19%), the 200-day at 1.66733 (-3.16%) and a 200-week average at 1.66591 that is still rising at 0.000773 per week, twenty weeks after the last weekly close above it. The dominant bilateral narrative is a 210bp carry deficit — an ECB deposit rate of 2.25% against an RBA cash rate of 4.35% — being harvested in a benign risk regime, with the euro leg's 10 September hike already 97% discounted while the Australian leg's 29 September decision remains a live 47-50% coin flip. The bilateral fact that most changes the standalone dossier views is that the Middle East energy shock, which each dossier scores as its own currency's largest structural negative, enters the two legs with opposite sign and therefore substantially cancels in the cross: TTF above EUR70/MWh taxes the world's largest net energy importer while paying a net energy exporter through coal at roughly US$130/t and Japanese LNG at US$19.0/mmbtu. The second is positioning, the one factor that amplifies rather than mutes — leveraged funds are short 60,600 euro contracts and long 54,061 Australian dollar contracts, the maximally short EUR/AUD configuration available to fast money. The settled verdict is tactically Bearish at conviction 2 (score -0.1102) and strategically Neutral at conviction 2 (+0.0503), and the direction is unusually well aligned with its funding, because a short is paid roughly 197bp annualised rather than charged. Our one substantive quarrel is that the tactical short has almost no downside real estate left — the 52-week low is 0.2% away and the 8-touch resistance shelf is 3.39% overhead — so the risk/reward on a fresh entry is materially worse than a -0.1102 score implies.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no pair-level PPP series. On the relative BIS real effective exchange rate proxy both dossiers use, the euro is 11.4% cheaper than the Australian dollar in real effective terms (102.69 against 115.92, both June 2026 observations), the widest gap in the euro's benchmark set after the yen. Australia's REER is the highest of the eleven currencies compared and follows a +10.36-point twelve-month real appreciation, more than double the next-largest move in the set, while nine of eleven economies saw their real rate fall. A commodity currency appreciating 10 REER points in a year while its own terms of trade fall 4.4% quarter-on-quarter to 111.90 is the configuration that historically precedes mean reversion. What is priced at 1.61459 is the full 210bp carry deficit, three delivered RBA hikes, an Australian AAA sovereign and an energy shock that pays the quote leg and taxes the base leg. What is not priced is any of the euro area's real-effective cheapness or the Australian dollar's real-effective richness — recorded as structural context and deliberately not scored, since real exchange rate extremes have essentially no timing power at two to four weeks and only weak power over one to six months.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral differential is -210bp: an ECB deposit rate of 2.25% against an RBA cash rate of 4.35%. On the consistent monthly sovereign basis the 10-year gap is -186.1bp. Annualised carry for a long EUR/AUD is -210bp; a rolled long pays away the differential and a rolled short collects it. The carry regime is textbook carry-supportive — VIX at 14.51, US investment grade at 79bp, high yield at 263bp and tightening — and in that tape the market funds in the 2.25% currency and buys the 4.35% one, which is the mechanical explanation for the pair's 9.03% twelve-month decline and its 0th closing percentile. The regime risk is symmetric and identifiable: a volatility shock reverses the ranking and mechanically supports the euro against the Australian dollar, because the Australian dollar's documented risk-off convexity is far worse than the euro's mid-beta, non-haven profile. Forward points, derived from the gated store's CME calendar-spread premium of +197.1bp annualised (observed 2026-08-31), are 12.9bp less than the 210bp policy differential, implying a basis contribution of roughly -13bp — small, benign, and independently corroborative of the minus-16-to-minus-20bp three-month EUR/USD basis reading in Factor 10. Structurally important: direction and carry point the same way for a bearish view in this pair, which is rare and materially improves the quality of the expression.

Trajectory inside the tactical window runs the other way, and it is a pricing story rather than a level story: the euro leg is spent, with the 10 September move to 2.50% discounted at roughly 97%, while the Australian leg is live, with about 47-50% priced for 4.60% on 29 September after three domestic confirmations in seventy-two hours in late August. The net for two to four weeks is that the only differential news arrives from Sydney, and it arrives nineteen days after Frankfurt's is already in the price.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential favours the Australian dollar and the activity differential favours the euro, and over two to four weeks the activity differential is the one that is moving. On inflation, Australia runs a trimmed mean of 3.6% and headline of 3.5% with services at 3.7%, against euro-area core of 2.5%, headline of 2.9% and services of 3.3% — an Australian core premium of roughly 110bp — and both are beating consensus, so the gap is stable rather than converging. On activity the level also favours Australia at 2.52% year-on-year against 1.0%, but the direction is emphatically euro-area: the German Ifo printed 88.8 against 87.2 expected, the flash composite 52.1 with new orders at a 40-month high, and German Q2 GDP beat at +0.3%, while Australia delivered unemployment at a post-COVID high of 4.5%, private capex -3.6% quarter-on-quarter against +0.8% expected, and NAB business confidence at -19. Transmission into the pair is asymmetric in the euro's favour precisely because Australia's data feeds the live RBA repricing: a soft Q2 national accounts print on 2 September, which the Australian dossier itself puts at roughly 40% for a sub-0.2% outcome, removes the marginal reason for a September hike, while the euro area's own August flash HICP on 1 September lands into a decision already 97% priced.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the growth differential is set to converge from below, which is the pair-positive direction. The euro area enters the horizon at 1.0% with a multi-year domestic demand floor under it — a EUR500bn infrastructure fund, defence spending heading to 3.5% of GDP — and an inflation composition that is imported rather than domestic. Australia enters at 2.52% with S&P forecasting a slowdown to 1.5% in fiscal 2027, a labour market at a post-COVID high of 4.5% unemployment, capex contracting and wages decelerating. So the differential narrows from -152bp toward roughly flat because the Australian side is weakening rather than because the euro side is accelerating. The offset, and the reason confidence is only 52, is that a stagflationary Australia is not reliably negative for the Australian dollar: sticky trimmed-mean inflation on a deteriorating growth base keeps the RBA hawkish, so the same data that closes the growth gap can also keep the 210bp carry deficit intact. The dated resolution is the Australian Q3 CPI in late October and the 3 November RBA Statement on Monetary Policy.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/AUD is a risk-OFF cross: it falls when global risk appetite is strong and rises when it is not, because the Australian dollar is the highest-beta risk and China proxy in the G10 while the euro is a non-haven mid-beta currency whose best environment is a benign, dollar-negative middle. The prevailing regime is close to the ideal configuration for the quote currency and only a good one for the base: VIX closed at 14.51, down 3.70 points on the month after touching a 2026 low of 14.2; US investment grade sits at 79bp and high yield at 263bp, 21bp tighter on the month; the Euro Stoxx 50 set a record above 6,560. In that tape the market funds in the low-yielder and buys the high-yielder, and the euro's own cross ranking confirms it — over the past month it gained against every haven and lost against every cyclical, including 1.37% against the Australian dollar. A distinctly bilateral flow reinforces it: Australian superannuation funds running roughly A$4.3trn hedge global equity allocations mechanically, so rising world equities force them to buy Australian dollars. The transmission is therefore not narrative but mechanical, and it points down for the pair.

The Australian dollar's documented risk-off behaviour is violent — a fall from roughly 0.80 to 0.55 against the dollar in weeks in 2020 — while the euro's non-haven status costs it against the dollar, franc and yen but not against a high-beta commodity currency. Net, a marginal positive with low confidence.

tactical.contrarian_case: The contrarian case is that the crowd is short this pair for reasons that are already fully in the price — a 210bp carry deficit that the forwards charge 197.1bp for, and an RBA repricing that has moved from 17% to 50% inside a week — while the reason the crowd could be forced out is not in the price at all: an Australian activity print that misses. A position built 95.8% larger in three weeks, at 18.2% of open interest, with dealers warehousing the other side, is a position whose exit is narrower than its entrance. The honest counterweight is that real money is already long the cross at 225,389 euro contracts and 45,427 Australian shorts, so the buyer who would benefit from the squeeze is already substantially positioned.

strategic.historical_analogue: Euro positioning squeezes are slow and grinding rather than violent because 800,000 contracts of open interest absorbs enormous flow before price moves, delivering three-to-five percent over months; Australian squeezes deliver comparable moves in weeks. In a cross, that mismatch means the Australian leg sets the timing and the euro leg sets the magnitude.
strategic.contrarian_case: The genuine strategic contrarian observation is that both structural shorts cannot be right simultaneously. If the energy shock persists, the Australian real-money short is wrong and the euro spec short is right, and the pair falls. If it resolves, the euro spec short is wrong and the Australian short is right, and the pair rises. Positioning therefore functions as an amplifier of whichever terms-of-trade outcome arrives rather than as an independent directional signal, which is why the strategic confidence here is 48 and not higher — and why the euro's declining reserve share, at 20.03% from 20.38% in a single quarter, is the more informative structural number than either futures book.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The world's largest net energy importer with no material commodity export offset. Natural gas (TTF) up is negative for the euro and is the critical single commodity for it; oil up is negative; LNG up is negative through the import bill. The euro benefits only from falling energy. Current readings: TTF above EUR70/MWh, storage 62.99%, energy HICP +10.0% year-on-year contributing +0.94pp of a 2.9% headline.

net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: TTF or LNG up ten percent: euro area minus-minus through the import bill, Australia plus through contract-linked coal and LNG receipts, so the pair FALLS — this is the dominant configuration today and it is why the same Middle East shock that both dossiers score as a negative for their own currency is not a negative for this cross. Iron ore down ten percent: Australia minus-minus on 35% of export revenue, euro area neutral to marginally positive as a steel-input importer, so the pair RISES. Oil up ten percent: euro area minus on the energy bill, Australia plus mildly on crude-linked LNG contracts, so the pair FALLS by roughly one to two percent on historical elasticities. Netting the current configuration — gas up, iron ore at the floor, oil down twelve percent in a month — leaves the two large forces close to offsetting, with the freshest impulse (gas) bearish for the pair and the most structural impulse (Simandou iron ore supply) bullish for it. The single conclusion that survives the netting is that EUR/AUD is the cleanest available expression in the G10 of a view that the energy supply shock resolves, because resolution collapses the euro area's import bill and Australia's export receipts simultaneously.

Brent from US$88.24 toward US$97 raises the euro area's import bill directly and lifts crude-linked Australian LNG contract pricing; it also keeps both central banks hawkish, which is a wash on the differential, so the terms-of-trade channel dominates and runs against the base currency.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair RISES approximately 1-2%. Brent toward US$79 relieves the euro area's largest external drag and simultaneously removes the conflict premium from Newcastle coal and Japanese LNG that Westpac already forecasts peaking this quarter. The complication is that it also removes the ECB's own stated inflation impulse, so the rate leg partially offsets the terms-of-trade gain.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Dutch TTF natural gas, with Japanese LNG as its transmission into the Australian leg. It is the euro's critical commodity, it is the direct channel through which the Hormuz closure reaches both currencies with opposite sign, and its dated test — the EU storage level on 1 November against 62.99% in August — is the highest-information variable in this factor. Iron ore is the second driver and works the other way, which is precisely why the strategic stance is Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks have been hawkish, both have been effective, and both have closed the gap between guidance and pricing to approximately zero, which is the definition of a Neutral guidance differential. The ECB's Account of the 22-23 July meeting, published 27 August, twice described the hold as a pause and stated it was important not to signal the end of the tightening cycle, and OIS moved to roughly 97% for 10 September within days. The RBA's 11 August statement was a unanimous hold that explicitly retained the sentence about increasing the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise, and the 25 August minutes disclosed that the Board debated a pre-emptive 25bp move. Sequencing is the one bilateral asymmetry and it partly favours the base: 10 September is a full projections round, so the euro leg has unpriced forecast content even though its decision does not, while 29 September carries no projection note. Set against that, the RBA's reaction function is more internally coherent — a unanimous vote against a euro-area Council whose President has conceded there is no clear evidence of second-round effects. The two cancel.

The market prices a 2.75% euro-area terminal by early 2027 against an ECB negotiated wage tracker printing 2.1% for Q2 2026 — down from 3.2% in 2025 — and against the Eurosystem's own projections showing headline inflation at 2.0% in 2028. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The dominant geopolitical variable enters this cross with opposite sign on each leg, which makes the pair an unusually clean instrument. The most recent flow is escalatory: on 31 August Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it downed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz and attacked a UAE air base, following Iranian strikes on US bases in Jordan. The one tactical offset on the Australian side is China, still in manufacturing contraction at 49.8. Net bearish for the pair, at low confidence because a single de-escalation headline reverses the sign.

The rate factor is the larger and it is negative for the pair: the euro pays 210bp less than the Australian dollar, the ECB's 10 September move to 2.50% is roughly 97% discounted and therefore spent, and the only live differential news inside the window arrives on 29 September at roughly 47-50% priced, after three domestic confirmations in seventy-two hours in late August — minutes disclosing a pre-emptive-hike debate, a July CPI beating consensus with the trimmed mean stuck at 3.6%, and household spending at +7.0% year-on-year. The inflation-and-growth factor pulls the other way for a genuinely different reason: the euro area is beating on activity while Australia is missing on it, with Ifo at 88.8 against 87.2 expected and new orders at a 40-month high against Australian capex at -3.6% quarter-on-quarter, construction at -2.1% and unemployment at a post-COVID 4.5%. The two standalone dossiers corroborate the direction mechanically rather than conflict with it: EUR scores +0.1359 tactically at rank 3 of 11 and AUD +0.2756 at rank 2, and the pair is the difference between them. Three bilateral facts modify those standalone views. First, this is a pure carry cross with no vehicle leg, so the differential is paid in full by a long — roughly 28 pips a month, a carry-to-vol ratio of -0.356 — and the direction and the funding therefore point the same way, which is rare and materially improves the quality of the bearish expression. Second, the same energy shock enters both legs with opposite sign, which neutralises what each dossier scores as a large negative for its own currency and leaves the terms-of-trade factor near zero strategically despite a 0.19 weight. Third, positioning is the one genuinely amplified bilateral signal and it runs against the score: leveraged funds are short 60,600 euro contracts and long 54,061 Australian dollar contracts, so the fast-money EUR/AUD short is doubled, and the Australian leg's crowding at 18.2% of open interest with dealers short 33,186 has a dated trigger while the euro leg's squeeze has already been collected. On priced versus expected the edge is narrow: both banks' guidance is fully absorbed, both dossiers' own analysts fade their own bank's front end, and the residual asymmetry is simply that only Sydney can be surprised inside the window. The path of least resistance is a lower pair while the risk regime holds, because VIX at 14.51 and high yield at 263bp mechanically favour the 4.35% currency over the 2.25% one. Dated catalysts: the euro-area August flash HICP and Australia's Q2 current account on 1 September, Australia's Q2 national accounts on 2 September, the ECB with projections on 10 September, the FOMC on 16 September and the RBA on 29 September. Conviction is 2 for three reasons: the score clears the threshold marginally, the largest positive for the pair argues directly against it, and a sub-0.2% Australian GDP print on 2 September — which the Australian dossier itself puts near 40% — would invert the rate factor's tactical asymmetry inside the first three sessions.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.0503 is Neutral by the mechanical rule and is functionally zero. The striking feature of the table is where the zeros sit: the two largest weights in the framework, Policy & Rates at 0.24 and External Balance at 0.19, contribute nothing at all — 43% of the total weight is genuinely balanced rather than lazily scored. Policy & Rates is zero because the differential is priced to end the horizon within 25bp of where it started, with a near-symmetric distribution around a midpoint the forwards already charge for. External Balance is zero because the same energy complex enters both legs with opposite sign, so escalation is doubly negative for the pair and resolution doubly positive, while the level of the two current accounts and the bilateral goods surplus run the other way. What is left is four modest positives — relative growth convergence, risk-distribution convexity, residual positioning and dollar-smile carry compression, totalling +0.1548 — against two modest negatives in Guidance and Fiscal totalling -0.1045. That is a genuinely balanced table, and the honest reading is that this pair has no strategic edge on relative policy and is instead a levered instrument on a single unresolved energy binary.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights 43% of the table sits in Policy & Rates and External Balance, and both score exactly zero, which is the most important thing in this synthesis and is not an evasion. The rate differential is priced to travel from -210bp to -185bp on 10 September and back to -210bp by 8 December if the RBA delivers its fully-priced move; on the February 2027 strip it ends at -185bp, a 25bp narrowing in the euro's favour that the 197.1bp forward premium already charges for, and the plausible range around it (-160bp to -235bp) is close to symmetric. Terms of trade cancel for a structural reason specific to this cross: the euro area is the world's largest net energy importer and Australia is a net energy and bulk-commodity exporter, so the Hormuz closure that pushed TTF above EUR70/MWh against 62.99% storage taxes the base leg and pays the quote leg through coal at roughly US$130/t and Japanese LNG at US$19.0/mmbtu, while the one-sided Australian negative — iron ore at US$95.34/t — largely arrives after this horizon closes. The two dossiers reinforce that symmetry rather than break it: both score their own External Balance as their largest strategic negative, and in a cross those two negatives substantially annihilate. What remains is a set of second-order differentials. Relative growth converges from below as Australia decelerates toward S&P's 1.5% fiscal-2027 forecast while the euro area stabilises on a German fiscal floor. The risk distribution from a VIX of 14.51 and high yield of 263bp is one-sided, and the Australian dollar's convexity to a shock is far worse than the euro's. The Federal Reserve is priced to add roughly 55-58bp against the RBA's 30bp, halving the Australian dollar's carry advantage over the dollar from +72.5bp toward +40bp while the euro's deficit stands still. Against those, guidance is the clearer negative for the pair: the market has extrapolated the ECB to a 2.75% terminal that its own 2.1% negotiated wage tracker and its own 2.0% 2028 inflation projection do not support, while the RBA's 4.60% is backed by a published path that keeps inflation above the midpoint until early 2028 on wages of 3.2%. Fiscal is the second negative and it is one-sided: Australia holds AAA from all three agencies on net debt near 20% of GDP with no review scheduled, while the base leg carries a French 2027 budget process running through this exact horizon with an explicit Fitch warning already published. On priced versus expected, the specific edge is that the market prices the ECB's hawkishness at face value and the Australian conflict premium as durable, and we think both are slightly wrong in the same direction for this cross. The path of least resistance is therefore sideways with a wide, energy-driven distribution rather than a trend. Dated catalysts: the Australian Q3 CPI in late October, the RBA Statement on Monetary Policy on 3 November, the EU gas storage reading on 1 November, the RBA on 8 December and the ECB projections round on 17 December. Conviction is 2 because a Neutral produced by two very large cancelling forces is less stable than one produced by an absence of forces, and either force winning decisively is worth several percent.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge by one notch and the gap is almost entirely mechanical, produced by two factor reversals and one reweighting. Policy & Rates goes from Bearish to Neutral because at two to four weeks what matters is which leg can still be repriced — only the Australian one can, since the ECB decision is 97% discounted nineteen days before the RBA's is half discounted — whereas over one to three months what matters is where the differential ends, and on the published paths it ends within 25bp of where it started with a near-symmetric distribution. External Balance goes from Bearish to Neutral while its weight rises from 0.09 to 0.19, because tactically the newest information is a euro-negative while strategically the two opposite-signed terms-of-trade shocks are properly weighed and cancel. Risk Appetite also flips, from Bearish on the prevailing regime to Bullish on the distribution of regimes. Guidance and Fiscal move the other way, from Neutral and low-confidence Bearish to firmer strategic negatives as the ECB's terminal credibility and the French budget process come into view.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October to early November 2026. Specifically the Australian Q3 CPI in the final week of October, which settles whether the July inflation acceleration was signal or noise, and the 3 November RBA decision with its quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy, which is the highest-signal Australian communication in the window. Once the Australian repricing is either delivered or withdrawn there is no further Australian policy news for at least a quarter, and the pair's driver rotates from the rate reaction function to the energy binary, the relative growth path and the Federal Reserve's compression of the Australian dollar's dollar-carry advantage. The window between the 29 September RBA and the late-October CPI is genuine no-man's-land in which neither thesis has an active catalyst. The price payload sharpens the handover: the tactical thesis needs to break 1.6106 and 1.61394 in the next four weeks; the strategic thesis needs nothing from price at all.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Carry the tactical bearish expression on a defined horizon that terminates at or before the 3 November RBA Statement on Monetary Policy, and do not roll it into the strategic window without re-underwriting Factor 5 against the 1 November EU gas storage reading. The alignment of direction and carry is the tactical advantage and it is horizon-agnostic — a short is paid roughly 197bp annualised either way — but the strategic Neutral is not a reason to hold that short by default; it is a reason to express the underlying views where each dossier says they are cleaner, and to treat any strategic position in this pair as a position on the energy shock resolving rather than on relative monetary policy.

The statement language matters as much as the decision — removing the sentence about increasing the cash rate target further would be a genuine dovish surprise into a market priced for the opposite, and sharply bullish for the pair.

catalysts.event: China official manufacturing PMI for September (August 49.8, from 49.2, new orders back above 50 at 50.6)
catalysts.rationale: The bilateral event-sensitivity asymmetry the framework asks for: a Chinese activity print matters enormously more to the quote leg than to the base leg, because China takes 30-35% of Australian exports and the Australian dollar is the most liquid G10 China proxy, while the euro area's exposure is a second-order trade channel. A relapse below 48.5 or new orders back under 49 pressures iron ore, already at US$95.34/t and the floor of its annual range, and lifts the pair; a move above 50.5 with orders holding does the reverse.

catalysts.event: Australia Q3 CPI, quarterly basis (approximate date; ABS publishes in the final week of October)
catalysts.rationale: The resolution event for the entire quote-leg thesis and therefore for the pair's cross-horizon divergence. Australia publishes headline and trimmed-mean CPI quarterly, which compresses three months of expectations into one number and produces outsized reactions. The Q2 print was 3.9% headline with a 3.6% trimmed mean. This settles the disagreement between the four houses that flipped to hike calls and Westpac's argument that the acceleration was noise, and it is the point at which the tactical bearish thesis either hands over to a firmer one or is withdrawn.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
catalysts.rationale: A non-projection meeting six weeks after the September move, so the language carries the information rather than the decision. The base case is a hold at 2.50%, and with the market pricing a 2.75% terminal by early 2027 the question is whether the hold is framed as another pause — which sustains the terminal and supports the base leg — or as data-dependent with softening wage commentary, which begins the downward repricing that Factor 6 identifies as the pair's clearest strategic negative.

catalysts.event: European Union gas storage fill level at 1 November — the physical test of the 62.99% reading recorded on 24 August, against an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information variable in the strategic table and the one that resolves the terms-of-trade cancellation in one direction or the other. Storage below 75% with TTF elevated taxes the base currency directly through the goods balance while sustaining Australian coal and LNG receipts — doubly negative for the pair, and Goldman has said current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage storage through winter with December TTF possibly needing to exceed EUR100/MWh. Storage above 85% with TTF easing does the reverse on both legs. Because the shock enters the two currencies with opposite sign, this single number is worth more to the cross than to either currency alone.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia decision with quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy
catalysts.rationale: The highest-signal quote-leg communication inside the strategic window and the tactical-to-strategic handover event. CBA, ANZ, Goldman Sachs and UBS all locate the hike to 4.60% here, and because the RBA signals through forecast revisions rather than explicit guidance, the accompanying Statement on Monetary Policy is where the terminal is set: the current vintage has underlying inflation at 3.3% by end-2026 with the midpoint not reached until early 2028. An upward revision opens a path beyond 4.60% and widens the pair's carry deficit; a downward revision closes the Australian cycle and removes the pair's largest single negative.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: An asymmetric configuration rather than a two-sided one: a hike to 4.60% by December is fully priced, so delivery is neutral for the pair and non-delivery is sharply bullish for it. This is also the date at which the bilateral differential mechanically returns to -210bp if the RBA delivers after the ECB's September move, which is the arithmetic behind the strategic Neutral on Factor 1. The meeting falls the day before the December FOMC, so the two decisions will be read together by the carry community.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff projections
catalysts.rationale: The pivotal base-leg event of the strategic horizon and the likeliest source of the repricing that makes Guidance the pair's clearest strategic negative. This is the first projection vintage in which the 2026 energy base effects enter the 2027 and 2028 forecast window clearly; a downward revision to the 2027 path removes the justification for the 2.75% terminal the market prices, against an ECB wage tracker already printing 2.1%. Because the Australian terminal has firmer domestic corroboration, a euro-area terminal repricing is not likely to be matched on the other leg.

catalysts.event: Status of the Strait of Hormuz and the US-Iran conflict, following the 31 August claim by Iran's Revolutionary Guard that it downed a US MQ-9 over the Strait and attacked a UAE air base
catalysts.rationale: Not a scheduled event, dated at the start of the window because it is a live condition rather than a release. It is the highest-impact variable for this specific cross and it is genuinely two-sided, because it enters the two legs with opposite sign: escalation raises the base currency's energy import bill while paying the quote currency through coal and LNG and reinforcing its central bank's hiking bias, and a durable ceasefire collapses both the base currency's import bill and the quote currency's export receipts at once. That symmetry is why the pair is the cleanest available G10 expression of a view on the shock resolving, and why Factor 7 is Neutral strategically despite the escalatory recent flow.

invalidators.condition: EUR/AUD posts a daily close above 1.62337 — the top of the six-touch pivot band it currently sits inside
invalidators.mechanism: The pair would have failed to break the 1.6106/1.61394 floor into the most favourable fundamental configuration available to a bearish view (a 97%-priced euro decision, a live Australian hike, VIX at 14.51 and TTF at a three-and-a-half-year high), and a failure to make new lows on that news set is the pair's own statement that the carry deficit is fully expressed.

invalidators.condition: Australian Q2 GDP prints below +0.2% quarter-on-quarter on 2 September and September RBA hike pricing falls below 25% from 47-50%
invalidators.new_stance: Neutral tactically, mildly Bullish for the pair
invalidators.mechanism: The -0.1440 Policy & Rates contribution rests entirely on the Australian leg being the only one with live repricing — remove that and the tactical score is +0.0338, a Neutral — and it would trigger the unwind of a leveraged long at 18.2% of Australian open interest into a dealer book short 33,186 contracts.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ABS national accounts and RBA-dated OIS
invalidators.monitor_frequency: single event, then daily on pricing

invalidators.condition: EU gas storage fails to reach 75% by 1 November and front-month TTF closes above EUR100/MWh on a weekly basis
invalidators.mechanism: This is the one condition that resolves the terms-of-trade cancellation decisively against the base leg — Europe buying scarce LNG at the margin while Australian coal and LNG receipts stay elevated is doubly negative for the pair, and it would take Factor 5 from a 0.19-weighted zero to roughly -0.15.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Aggregated Gas Storage Inventory EU fill level and ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement

invalidators.condition: A durable US-Iran ceasefire reopens the Strait of Hormuz with TTF below EUR40/MWh on a monthly average and Brent below US$70
invalidators.mechanism: Resolution collapses the base currency's import bill and the quote currency's export receipts simultaneously — the doubly positive branch — and would put the eight-touch 1.6619-1.6767 shelf in play, 3.39% above spot.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month, Brent front-month, ceasefire headlines

invalidators.condition: Iron ore 62% Fe CFR records five consecutive settlements below its US$93.66 fifty-two-week low
invalidators.new_stance: Bullish for the pair at both horizons
invalidators.mechanism: Iron ore is roughly 35% of Australian export revenue and is the one commodity leg in this cross with no offsetting exposure on the euro side — a confirmed break with Simandou supply of roughly 20Mt arriving would convert the Australian terms-of-trade decline from cyclical to structural.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Iron ore 62% Fe CFR futures settlement

invalidators.condition: Euro-area terminal-rate pricing falls below 2.50% at any point after 10 September while the Australian terminal holds at or above 4.60%
invalidators.mechanism: It removes the only credibility asymmetry the base leg has left — the -0.0660 Guidance contribution already assumes the euro terminal is 15-25bp too high, and confirmation of that would widen the differential toward -235bp rather than the -185bp the forwards charge for.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Euro-area OIS terminal pricing and the 29 October and 17 December ECB statement language

invalidators.condition: CFTC prints show the Australian leveraged net long above +65,000 contracts while the euro non-commercial short re-extends beyond -70,000
invalidators.new_stance: Reduce tactical conviction to Neutral regardless of price
invalidators.mechanism: That is the amplified EUR/AUD short reaching the zone from which Australian dollar reversals have historically originated, on a float of only 333,906 contracts against the euro's 801,884 — a squeeze from there is mechanically violent and the pair has an 85-pip air pocket to its four-touch support with no threshold-qualifying zone below it.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Commitments of Traders, both taxonomies
invalidators.monitor_frequency: weekly, Friday for the prior Tuesday

invalidators.condition: EUR/AUD closes above the 200-day moving average at 1.66733 on a weekly basis
invalidators.new_stance: Bullish at both horizons, ends the thesis entirely
invalidators.mechanism: That level also sits inside the eight-touch 1.6619-1.6767 shelf and 14 pips above the rising 200-week average at 1.66591 — clearing all three simultaneously would end a twenty-week regime below the long-term average and turn systematic flow buyer in a cross where nothing that met the two-touch threshold sits between there and the 1.76227 band.

signposts.indicator: EUR/AUD 1.6106-1.62337 pivot band and the 52-week closing low at 1.61394
signposts.current_level: spot 1.61459, inside the band, 6.5 pips above the annual closing low
signposts.invalidates_if: a daily close above 1.62337, or any close above the 50-day at 1.63603
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only level in either leg's technical picture that is about the cross itself. Neither the euro's own support nor the Australian dollar's own resistance says anything about the relative price, and a six-touch band that spot sits inside — with its lower bound 5 pips from the 52-week intraday low — is where the entire tactical thesis is either delivered or refused.

signposts.indicator: RBA-dated hike probability for 29 September and the EUR-AUD policy differential
signposts.current_level: approximately 47-50% for 4.60% on 2026-09-29; differential -210bp; roughly 30bp cumulative priced to February 2027
signposts.confirms_if: September probability rises above 65%, or cumulative priced Australian tightening to February 2027 exceeds 45bp while euro-area terminal pricing holds at or below 2.50%
signposts.invalidates_if: September probability falls below 25%, or the differential narrows inside -185bp on delivered policy
signposts.bilateral_importance: Matters more for this pair than for either currency alone because EUR/AUD is a pure carry cross with no vehicle leg — the forward premium of 197.1bp is 94% of the policy gap, so basis contributes almost nothing and repricing transmits into spot almost one-for-one.

signposts.indicator: EU gas storage fill level and Dutch TTF front-month
signposts.current_level: EU storage 62.99% at end of gas day 24 August 2026; TTF above EUR70/MWh on 31 August, highest since January 2023
signposts.confirms_if: storage below 75% on 1 November with TTF above EUR85/MWh — doubly negative for the pair
signposts.invalidates_if: storage above 85% on 1 November with TTF below EUR55/MWh, and decisively if TTF falls below EUR40/MWh
signposts.bilateral_importance: The single highest-information variable in the entire analysis, and it matters only in a cross like this one. For the euro alone gas is a negative; for the Australian dollar alone it is a positive; in EUR/AUD the two compound rather than offset, so one number moves both legs in the same direction for the pair.

signposts.current_level: US$95.34/t against a 52-week range of US$93.66-111.42 — at the floor
signposts.confirms_if: sustained above US$105/t, restoring Australian terms of trade above 115
signposts.bilateral_importance: The only commodity in this cross with exposure on one leg and none on the other. Every energy price nets between the two currencies; iron ore does not, because roughly 35% of Australian export revenue depends on it while the euro area is a marginal steel-input importer.

signposts.indicator: Combined CFTC positioning: euro non-commercial net and Australian leveraged-fund net
signposts.current_level: euro non-commercial -36,352 contracts (report 25 August); Australian leveraged funds +54,061 (16.2%-18.2% of OI); Australian legacy non-commercial -44.5k, unreconciled
signposts.confirms_if: the Australian leveraged long falls below +45,000 while the pair falls, or the euro short re-extends beyond -50,000
signposts.invalidates_if: the Australian leveraged long exceeds +65,000, or the euro short converts toward flat and above
signposts.bilateral_importance: The only factor in this analysis where the two legs amplify rather than mute. Short the base and long the quote is the maximally short EUR/AUD configuration available to fast money, so the pair-level crowding is roughly double what either leg's own dossier reports.
signposts.frequency: weekly, Friday release for the prior Tuesday

signposts.indicator: EUR/AUD 3-month ATM implied volatility estimate versus 60-day realised
signposts.current_level: 5.892% at 94.7 days (estimate) against 4.85% 60-day realised; term structure 5.588%/5.892%/6.170% in clean contango; ATR(14) 74 pips
signposts.confirms_if: realised volatility rises above 6.0% while the pair falls — a trending break rather than a range grind
signposts.invalidates_if: realised volatility falls below 4.0% with the pair holding inside 1.6106-1.62337
signposts.bilateral_importance: The pair's own surface is the only place where the market prices the interaction of the two legs' event calendars, and it is pricing nothing: no hump in front of an ECB projections round and a near-coin-flip RBA decision nineteen days apart.

signposts.indicator: Germany 10-year Bund minus Australia 10-year ACGB spread
signposts.current_level: -186.1bp on the consistent monthly basis; approximately -178bp on live dossier levels — cross-date approximation
signposts.confirms_if: the deficit widens beyond -200bp on live levels
signposts.invalidates_if: the deficit narrows inside -150bp, most plausibly on a Bund term-premium extension
signposts.bilateral_importance: The term-structure counterpart to the policy differential, capturing what the two curves think about the two terminals rather than what the two front ends currently pay. Both 2s10s slopes are +39bp, identically flat, so any move in this spread is a level move rather than a shape move.
signposts.frequency: daily on live levels, monthly on the consistent series

signposts.current_level: 49.8 in August 2026, up from 49.2, still in contraction; new orders 50.6
signposts.confirms_if: the headline holds above 50.5 for two consecutive months with new orders above 51
signposts.invalidates_if: the headline falls below 48.5 or new orders return below 49
signposts.bilateral_importance: A classic bilateral asymmetry: China takes 30-35% of Australian exports and the Australian dollar is the most liquid G10 China proxy, while the euro area's exposure is a second-order trade channel. A Chinese activity print therefore moves this cross almost entirely through one leg.
signposts.frequency: monthly, released on the final day of the reference month

assumptions: Convention: EUR/AUD is quoted as Australian dollars per euro. Every stance in this report is expressed as the PAIR rising or falling; no single-currency stance appears without conversion to a pair direction.

Two-pass structure: pass 1 scored the ten factors and set both stances without access to the price payload, deliberately, so that a stance could not be reverse-engineered from a chart. All ten factor blocks and the entire synthesis analytical text are reproduced unchanged from pass 1; everything price-derived is pass 2's own work.

Where we disagree with the settled direction: we do not disagree with the tactical Bearish label — the score is -0.1102 and the rule is mechanical — but we disagree with how much runway it has, given the pair is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week closing range with an eight-touch resistance shelf 3.39% overhead and only 85 pips of four-touch support below.

Price payload provenance: dataPoints 130; dateRange 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03; computationRange 2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03 (4,879 weekday bars); spot 1.61459; spotDate 2026-09-03; only 6 resistance / 2 support zones met the 2-touch threshold.

Spot date gap: spotDate is 2026-09-03, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date and after both dossiers' own 2026-08-28 price anchors. Every level, target, stop, and distance in this report is computed against 1.61459, and no fresher web quote was substituted.

Moving averages: SMA50 1.63603, SMA100 1.63408, SMA200 1.66733, SMA200w 1.66591 are simple averages of trading-day closes computed over the whole stored history of 4,879 weekday bars. The 200-week average's forward projection is our own linear extrapolation of the stated slope and is labelled as such.

Performance figures: the payload's pre-calculated 1M/3M/6M/1Y figures are quoted verbatim; across the 130 visible bars the pair fell 2.24%, which exceeds the stated six-month figure of -0.18% because the six-month anchor is not the first visible bar — the discrepancy is disclosed rather than reconciled.

Support and resistance: all zones come from the payload's computed zones; no support or resistance level was web-searched. Because only two support zones met the two-touch threshold, the support side is supplemented with round numbers and one externally-sourced, unverified Fibonacci projection at 1.5359.

Implied volatility is an estimate, not a quote: EUR/AUD has no listed option; the 5.588/5.892/6.170 curve is derived from the variance identity fed a realised correlation of 0.6378 standing in for an unobservable implied one, with a documented median 14.4% understatement. Risk reversals, butterflies and a quoted IV percentile are documented gaps and no directional inference is drawn from skew.

Forwards are derived, not quoted: the 1M/3M/6M outrights are computed from the payload's CME calendar-spread premium of +197.1bp annualised applied linearly to spot on an actual/365 basis; the -12.9bp residual against the 210bp policy gap is attributed to basis as an inference.

Rates: both 10-year yields in the payload are monthly series as of 2026-06-01 and are never quoted here as live levels; live levels in the text come from the two dossiers with their own dates, and the resulting -178bp figure is a cross-date approximation.

Bilateral trade: IMF Direction of Trade Statistics for 2024, two years stale at the valuation date; the two reported directions differ by USD 1.6bn on mirror-statistics grounds and neither was adjusted, used as structural characterisation rather than current flow measurement.
Weight adjustments: three factors adjusted, all within the ±0.05 limit, all justified bilaterally, both tables summing to exactly 1.00 (Factor 3 +0.01, Factor 5 +0.03, Factor 10 -0.04).

Web research scope and exclusions: four targeted searches were run; algorithmic extrapolation sites returning multi-year daily EUR/AUD 'forecasts' were excluded as a category error. No web source was used for spot, performance, moving averages, realised volatility or support and resistance levels.

Inherited staleness carried with its flags: BIS REER June 2026 observations; ECB negotiated wage tracker dated 17 June 2026; 3-month EUR/USD basis mid-May 2026; Australian federal net debt figure flagged best-available; Australian Q1 current account 91 days old; a late-August Newcastle coal print could not be re-confirmed.

Calendar: all scheduled EUR and AUD central bank dates come from the gated calendar file; the Australian Q3 CPI date and the 2026-09-30 China PMI are not in the gated calendar and are flagged as approximate.

Judgements disclosed: all scenario probabilities, tail probabilities and invalidator probabilities are the author's structured estimates, not market-implied figures; each scenario set sums to 100%. Position sizing arithmetic is illustrative and assumes no leverage constraint.
